title: The Pentagon-Silicon Complex and the Rise of the Neo-Primes
gist: Podcast episode description only: Sharon Weinberger, new editor-in-chief of the Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists, discusses her book Valley of Death on how Big Tech fuels future war, the Pentagon's disputes with SpaceX and Anthropic, and how new firms could become the next defense primes ('neo-primes').

insights.claim: The U.S. military increasingly depends on technologies it does not own, a dependency illustrated by the Pentagon's disputes with SpaceX and Anthropic.
insights.speaker: Sharon Weinberger and Jonathan Panter
insights.so_what: Vendor leverage over the Pentagon creates both pricing power and political/contract risk for tech suppliers.
insights.quote: What happens when the military depends on technologies it doesn’t own?
insights.locator: What happens when the military depends

insights.claim: Sharon Weinberger argues the tech industry's split from the military was driven more by money than by ideology.
insights.speaker: Sharon Weinberger and Jonathan Panter
insights.so_what: If economics drove the split, larger defense budgets can readily pull tech firms back into defense work.
insights.quote: why the tech industry’s split from the military was about money more than ideology
insights.locator: What happens when the military depends

insights.claim: A new generation of technology firms could become the next defense primes, forming a 'Pentagon-Silicon complex.'
insights.speaker: Sharon Weinberger and Jonathan Panter
insights.so_what: Watch defense-tech challengers potentially displacing legacy primes in contract share.
insights.quote: how a new generation of firms could become the next primes
insights.locator: What happens when the military depends
